name: cloudy-apps-communication-mcp
description: Mail MCP server — IMAP/SMTP/Admin via Stalwart REST API

deploy._doc_excludes: #1802: data/ holds the delivery-status ledger (delivery-ledger.jsonl, bind-mounted at /data). The deploy rsync must never delete or overwrite it.

proxied_mcps._note: URLs resolved at flake build time from cloud-data services{}. Bridge mode → WG IPs only. Same retry/LRU pattern as cloud-services-mcp.

_env_note: env_file must carry the mail vars (MADDY_ME_*/MAIL_*, RESEND, STALWART) AND the mattermost vars (MM_URL, MM_CLAUDE_PASSWORD, MM_TEAM_ID, MM_ADMIN_USERNAME).
_dns_doc: The old container keeps these DNS names during the alias release; move them here (dns_aliases) at cutover when the old container is removed.

runtime._why_oom_score_adj: #1659: every MCP server on oci-apps is in the last tier the kernel OOM killer picks (_shared/oom-priority.json, tier mcp). Restart policy is 'no' (owner rule), so a killed MCP stays down and its tools are gone until someone starts it by hand. -900 = the host's connectivity tier; not -1000, which would also exempt it from its own cgroup limit.

secrets._doc: Values only in the private vault at Linux-Containers/infra-api_cloudy-apps-communication-mcp/src/secrets.yaml (sops, public fleet recipient; the Ship overlay copies it in, the engine mounts .secrets as env_file and the /run/secrets mounts). It is the UNION of the two files it replaces, copied verbatim (never generated): Linux-Containers/infra-api_cloud-mail-mcp/src/secrets.yaml and Linux-Containers/infra-api_cloud-mattermost-mcp/src/secrets.yaml. Keys by NAME, listed in _keys; no `required` list on purpose, so nothing generates a placeholder for a real password. The server exits at start without MADDY_ME_USER+MADDY_ME_PASSWORD or MAIL_USER+MAIL_PASSWORD.

delivery_api._doc: #1802 + #1803 REST surface of the fleet mail API, served by this same Node process ahead of the MCP transport (src/code/mcp/delivery; contract: DELIVERY-API.md). Same auth as the MCP: WG-mesh-only (Caddy wg_only + listener bound to the oci-apps WG IP). The ledger is fed by Stalwart itself (user-comm_tools-stalwart build.json#delivery_ledger: WebHook + MtaHook to /v1/internal/stalwart/*), accepted only from ingest_allowed. relay_hosts are next hops that are relays (OCI Email Delivery, the Maddy leg), so their 250 is recorded as 'accepted by relay' (pending), never as delivered. Mailbox probes run from this host: OCI blocks outbound TCP/25, so a remote-MX probe reports mailbox=unknown with the connect error; local domains are probed at Stalwart's own SMTP over wg0 (probe_overrides).

probe._doc_budgets: timeout_ms = the whole SMTP dialogue after connect; connect_timeout_ms = the TCP connect; request_budget_ms = the whole POST /v1/recipients/check (unfinished checks answer unknown). canary_host: one TCP connect (no SMTP command) decides, cached recheck_ms, whether outbound :25 works from this host; while it does not, remote MX probes are skipped instantly (OCI drops outbound :25).

_status: #1450: standard service (flake, compose, ship engine link); replaces cloud-mail-mcp + cloud-mattermost-mcp, takes port 3103 over at deploy (engine port eviction).
